title: Support to mock socket in ReadinessService to improve testability

timeline.message:
Support to mock socket in ReadinessService to improve testability

The mocked socket allows to avoid issues due to ephemeral port re-use by testing open/close socket directly instead that through a connection.
In this first iteration, the injection of the mocked sockets happens by overriding the socket "open" method, which is static. The "open" method is abstracted through a static Supplier,  defaulting to current implementation. The field is package private.
Using and updating a static field have multiple problems (concurrency, time of set vs time of use, etc.). Following iterations will explore better alternatives.
timeline.author: Lorenzo Dematte

timeline.body:
The mock allows to avoid issues due to ephemeral port re-use by testing open/close status by probing the mocked "socket" class directly, instead of trying to open a connection with a TCP client. 

The injection of the mocked sockets happens by overriding the socket `open` method, which is static. 
In this first iteration, the "open" method is abstracted through a static Supplier, defaulting to the real `ServerSocketChannel::open` implementation. The field is static and package private. 

Using and updating a static field have multiple problems (concurrency, time of set vs time of use, etc.). Following iterations will explore better alternatives.

timeline.message: Using MockNode/TestPlugin pattern for better integration with test framework
timeline.author: Lorenzo Dematte

timeline.body: Second iteration: I have changed the way mocked sockets are injected by following the approach adopted by existing mocked services (e.g. `MockSearchService` and `MockScriptService`), by creating a `MockReadinessService` and instantiating it in `MockNode` through a `newReadinessService` factory method in `Node`.

Shouldn't this be a ConcurrentHashMap since many threads could be involved? At minimum the readiness service running in a different thread than the test itself that asserts on the socket state.

reply.body: Good catch, I had a simple map initially and made a mental note to review that.. and forgot. Will fix.

timeline.body: We should override close as well, which should remove the socket from the static map? Otherwise the same node name used across different tests could have unexpected results?

reply.body: I cannot remove these in close, as these mocks are used to hold the information of the socket status for that node (much like `ReadinessService.boundAddress()` in the current version of the tests). But you are right, the static map is a problem as node names could clash. I will find a better alternative.

I realized that since we have a `MockReadinessService` to rely on now (as opposed to the first draft were I was trying to use mockito) we don't even need the map anymore: the socket (mocked) is there, so we can avoid some boilerplate and be much closer to the original way of testing. Thanks for pointing this out and making me "look harder".

reply.body: I like this idea, it's a nice improvement. Also, I suspect that if we track the bound address in the mock, we can get rid of some internal methods on ReadinessService itself (like, boundAddress()) which appears to be there/to be package private just for testing purposes. I think we should try to move these assertions on the mocked socket.

timeline.body: I think we still want to override close() so that we can know if eg accept() is called after we close when shutting down?

reply.body:
This is surely a good thing to do, and the best thing is that we don't even need to do that: close is not overridable (final in `AbstractInterruptibleChannel`); the hierarchy does offer a template method to override (`implCloseSelectableChannel`), but `close` `open` etc. already keep track of the channel status in a `closed` field (exposed by `isOpen`). We can `assert isOpen()` (or throw a AssertException) in accept too.

If we add other state (e.g. not open/closed but just _not_ shut down, or the bound address you were mentioned above, or else), then it would be useful to override `implCloseSelectableChannel` to record that/clean state up. I will keep it in mind.

timeline.body: This looks much simpler, thanks for the changes. I think this is a good start for a mock socket. I think there are some more things we may want to mock within the socket (eg accept) so that we can further improve the tests, but those can happen as followups. I left some ideas.

> I think there are some more things we may want to mock within the socket (eg accept) so that we can further improve the tests, but those can happen as followups.

I surely agree with you. Initially I added things like tracking bind and accept (similar to what you suggested), but then kept it minimal for our test case. I did it on purpose, to separate the 2 things: replace the current implementation keeping the same tests, then when we see the new thing is working, improve. 
It's also learning how things are done in ES for me too: I would follow up with 2 PRs here: 
- getting rid of ReadinessClientProbe (and real sockets) in ReadinessServiceTests 
- improve tests by asserting state (and therefore capturing more state)

But if you think that doing all in one PR is more suitable to the way we work, let me know and I will adjust my workflow! (suggestions welcome @rjernst)
